steps.note: exchange-network.md fixes h=100, v=C(h,3)=161700, banks X_a,Y_a indexed by a in T^3, N=v^3, m=h^3=10^6 ('dimension of the label space used later'), gives the gather/scatter/side-wire invocation, the three stages giving (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), i.e. (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), restoring every scratch wire whatever its initial value, and the wire counts W_b, W_c. All match paper 640-783. Reason: the page calls it 'the finite building block of the later tape procedures', and its 'Where this fits' box places it in the plan (network + frames so each edge costs one smaller call per unit of rank, total rank s<Wm, recurrence). The page itself does not say why restoring arbitrary scratch values matters later; address-interchange.md supplies that (scratch rows also receive H<-H+D).

array-frames.md states the frame D_v per source/gate/sink, common to all incidences of a gate, the commutation G(D_v g_1..)=D_v G(g_1..) by R-linearity, the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, the telescoping to endpoint frames on each route, and that an edge costs whatever applying D_v D_u^{-1} costs, matching paper 793-843. Reason is explicit in 'What the free frames are for': interior frames are free, so they can be chosen to make each edge cheap, which the subspace-labels page does and the recursion counts. Minor looseness: it says the labels page 'uses nested subspaces as frames' (the frames are matrices/permutations built from the labels), not a contradiction.

subspace-labels.md gives the bit form x.y-(1/9)(x.1)(y.1) on Q^h and the dot product on F_2^h, nondegenerate triple lines with neighbours orthogonal, labels in F^{otimes3} of dimension h^3=m, terminal labels (U_a/F, 0/U_a-perp, 0/F), the stage notation [G|E], the stage transitions, and the full gate-time table 0..7 for centre, side, X, Y wires; it states every arrow is an inclusion except centre 3->4, which drops P(x)F(x)Q of dimension h, and that all labels are nondegenerate. Checked against paper 845-1010 (gate-label table 975-988, Lemma 997-1010): consistent. Reason: labels choose the frames so the network costs s<Wm smaller calls, 'the saving the recursion needs'; 'to save, the labels must confine all loss to one small edge'.

subspace-labels.md assigns projection Pi_U to a vertex labelled U, -Pi_{U_a} to source X_a and 0 to other sources, proves that for nondegenerate U in U' the difference Pi_{U'}-Pi_U projects onto U' cap U-perp and has rank dim U'-dim U (same for the reversed edge), and singles out the N first X_a edges: zero dimension change but matrix 2Pi_{U_a} of rank one. Matches paper 1156-1166. Reason: the preceding paragraph says each matrix gives a frame that shears one address chunk by another, so an edge costs one smaller call per unit of rational rank; rank=dimension change is what lets the label budget count the calls.

subspace-labels.md: source dimensions sum to N, sink dimensions to Nm+N(m-1)+(W-2N)m=Wm-N, signed changes telescope at gates to Wm-2N, absolute changes Wm-2N+2L, L_b=I c_b h (L=Ich), and s_b=(W_b m-2N+2L_b)+N=W_b m-N+2L_b. Matches paper 891-897, 997-1010, 1138-1154. rank-recurrence.md restates the budget intuitively (the 2N bank saving, 2L to regain losses, +1 rank per X_a sign). Reason: s is the number of smaller calls the recursion pays. Small imprecision only in hover text: the subspace-labels one-line definition calls 'the total dimension change over edges' the number s, which for the bit network omits the +N source ranks; the page body is correct.

subspace-labels.md computes L_b/N=3c_b h/v=30000/161700=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, and the deficit W_b m-s_b=N-2L_b=(339/539)N>0, hence s_b<W_b m (and s_c<W_c m), with the relative deficit 339/22587335000000. Matches paper 1105-1110, 1166-1167. Reason: rank-recurrence.md explains that s=Wm would give cost proportional to Vf (no saving) and that any positive deficit puts the exponent below 1.

subspace-labels.md: 'The negative source makes every route's endpoint difference Id, the same shear on every role: Pi_{U_a-perp}+Pi_{U_a} from X_a to Y_a, Pi_F-0 elsewhere' (compressed but with the defining content). address-interchange.md states M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m, reads inputs as Phi_{-M_in} f_w, derives f'_{rho(w)}=Phi_{I_m} f_w, and concludes H<-H+D on every original row including scratch rows with arbitrary initial values; then the outer updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D give the interchange. Matches paper 1138-1172 and 1514-1541. Reason given: it explains why the negative source (and its extra rank) is needed and what the uniform shear makes possible (the chunk interchange).

matrix-shear.md gives A=E_1 Pi E_2 with E_1,E_2 invertible lower triangular and Pi with exactly rank(A) ones (elimination proof), reduction mod q^b, triangular parts in O(V) by controlled shifts, and each one of Pi done with one interchange via D_j<-D_j+H_i, swap, D_j<-H_i-D_j, so exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Matches paper 1364-1447. address-interchange.md applies it per edge and states 'The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly s'. Reason: the 'Where this fits' box on matrix-shear.md (an edge of rank a costs a interchanges of 1/m width, giving F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)) and the prose of address-interchange.md and rank-recurrence.md. Thin spot, not a break: matrix-shear.md sits in Part 3, before the network and labels in reading order, so a linear reader meets it before knowing what an edge matrix is; the box covers this.

address-interchange.md: rows split into W role streams of volume V/W, F_0=O(1), F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), geometric sum with c=s/W<m^tau in both cases c<=1 and c>1, F_k=O(e^tau), tau=1-2^{-50} chosen because eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20. rank-recurrence.md gives the same recurrence in per-unit-volume form, the explicit eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500, and the tangent-line argument m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta)=s/W. Matches paper 1319-1346, 1475-1557. Reason: both pages say this is what makes the interchange (and the layer) cost the volume times a power below one of the width, which the later transform layout and cost accounting use.

links.note: exchange-network.md links to array-frames.md in its Connections diagram and 'Used by' list (not in body prose); array-frames.md links back in prose and in 'Before this page'. Part 4 index orders them 1 then 2.
array-frames.md prose: 'The later page [Nested subspace labels and rank deficit](subspace-labels.md) makes this choice', plus Connections and 'Used by'.
Both on subspace-labels.md: the gate-label table and decreasing-edge claim, then the projection matrices and the rank=dimension-change argument.
subspace-labels.md: the budget Wm-2N+2L is stated before C4 and completed after it as s_b=(W_b m-2N+2L_b)+N.
subspace-labels.md computes L/N=100/539 and 101/539 and the deficit N-2L_b next to the budget; rank-recurrence.md repeats both.

subspace-labels.md states the endpoint identity right after s_b<W_b m. The explicit 'H<-H+D on every role' is on address-interchange.md, reached from subspace-labels.md via rank-recurrence.md (indirect), but C7's defining content is already on subspace-labels.md.

address-interchange.md states the endpoint identity (I_m on every role, H<-H+D on every row) and the edge-shear cost (rank many interchanges plus O(V), s recursive calls in all), with a prose link to matrix-shear.md for the E_1 Pi E_2 factorization. From subspace-labels.md alone the route to matrix-shear.md would be indirect, via rank-recurrence.md.

address-interchange.md goes from 'exactly s' recursive calls on V/W streams to F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and F_k=O(e^tau); matrix-shear.md's 'Where this fits' box and Connections also link to address-interchange.md.

summary: Yes: W1 carries a reader from the fixed exchange network to the exponent tau. exchange-network.md, array-frames.md and subspace-labels.md reconstruct C1-C7 with their defining content and stated purpose, linked in order, and address-interchange.md with matrix-shear.md and rank-recurrence.md turns edge ranks into s recursive calls and solves F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) to O(e^tau) with tau=1-2^{-50}, all consistent with the paper. Nothing breaks the chain; it thins out in a few places: subspace-labels.md is very dense and states the endpoint identity in a single sentence, the shear lemma sits earlier in reading order than the network it serves, and the one-line hover definition of subspace labels leaves out the N extra source ranks in s_b.
